intro: Trinidad and Tobago is a two-island nation off Venezuela, birthplace of calypso, soca and the steelpan.

chapters.title: Spanish and British rule
text: Columbus named Trinidad in 1498. Spain held it lightly; Britain took Trinidad in 1797, and Tobago changed hands many times before becoming British. Sugar and cocoa plantations used enslaved Africans.

chapters.title: Indenture
text: After slavery ended, about 144,000 indentured workers came from India between 1845 and 1917, so today the population is roughly equal parts African and Indian descent.

highlight.title: Two heritages
highlight.text: Diwali and Carnival are both national celebrations.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Trinidad and Tobago became independent in 1962 under Eric Williams and a republic in 1976. Oil and gas made it one of the Caribbean's richest countries.

keyTerms.meaning: A drum made from an oil barrel, tuned to play notes.
